editorial_title_zh: 周末想去！走近禅世界的展览：禅与吉卜力、大德寺、白隐世界等，不妨带走能活用于日常生活与工作的禅语和教诲
editorial_excerpt_zh: 以不仅在日本、亦受到世界瞩目的“禅”为主题的展览正在各地举办。从汇聚京都数一数二禅宗寺院至宝的瞩目大展，到通过动画作品轻松走近禅世界的展览，阵容丰富多彩。禅

article_text:
日本のみならず、世界からの注目も集まる「禅」をテーマとした展覧会が各地で開催されています。京都有数の禅宗寺院の至宝が一堂に介する注目展から、アニメ作品を通して気軽に禅の世界に親しめる展覧会まで、多彩なラインナップです。禅に対して難解なイメージを抱く方も多いかと思いますが、心惹かれる作品や親近感がわく書画などを通して、その世界に気軽に触れてみてはいかがでしょう。日常や仕事にも活きる禅の言葉、教えを持ち帰ることができるかもしれません。

開創700年記念 特別展「大徳寺 本朝無双之禅苑」 東京国立博物館で12月6日まで 洛北の巨刹の歴史を物語る至宝の数々が一堂に

「白隠ワールド―細川護立コレクションのはじまり―」東京・永青文庫で11月29日まで 白隠の世界にどっぷりはまる

『禅とジブリ』京都展 京都市京セラ美術館 新館 東山キューブで12月6日まで ジブリ作品の世界に没入しながら禅の言葉と視点を自由に持ち帰る

「良寛さん―その人と禅―」京都・細見美術館で11月8日まで 慈愛と禅の精神が詰まった珠玉の作品群にふれる

秋の企画展 大本山 佛通寺展 ふくやま草戸千軒ミュージアム（広島県立歴史博物館）で11月29日まで まもなく創建630周年を迎える佛通寺の貴重な文化財を紹介

◇あわせて読みたい

【座談会】「この世は美しかった」と旅立つために――医科大学がリベラルアーツセンターを開く理由とは 京都の禅宗寺院の妙心寺退蔵院で歴史学者、禅僧、医師がトーク【PR】

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）

title_original: Sacred Monsters
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在布鲁克林的 Picto New York，皮克托纽约正在呈现“妖怪与风景”（Yōkai and Landscapes），这是渡边裕司在美国的首次个人展览。这位常年往返于巴黎和东京的日本摄影师，将用宝丽来拍摄的日本民间传说中的生灵与荒凉的风景置于对话之中……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "日本民俗学之父柳田国男曾写道：“妖怪是坠落的神明。”这句话曾伴随渡边裕司 2024 年 9 月在东京 229 画廊举办的展览“Yōkai”，并且它打开了所有的门。一个被击落神坛的神明，随后被驱逐出神社，在折屏后面、在褪色的和服里、在旧被褥下寻求庇护。这是从神坛跌落的惨烈。按字面意思来说，它们是神圣的怪兽。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "渡边裕司深知蜕变的力量。他在日本接受培训，在纽约学习摄影，回到东京，随后于 2012 article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“A yōkai is a fallen god,” wrote Yanagita Kunio, the father of Japanese folklore studies. The line already accompanied Yuji Watanabe’s exhibition “Yōkai” at 229 Gallery in Tokyo in September 2024, and it opens every door. A god knocked off his pedestal, then, driven out of the shrines, taking refuge behind folding screens, in faded kimonos, under old futons. A harsh fall from grace. Sacred monsters, in the literal sense."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Yuji Watanabe knows the power of metamorphosis. Trained in Japan, he studied photography in New York, returned to Tokyo, then settled in Paris in 2012. He shoots fashion stories for international magazines, a world where a coat is enough to change a silhouette (creatures demand more). Alongside it grew a personal practice, analog and stubborn. As he explains, the fantastic needs the real in order to exist: without that share of reality at the moment of creation, he himself stops feeling the fantastic, hence his attachment to analog processes. The large-format camera, the light, the chemistry, all of it."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-miku-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Miku © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-boroboroton-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Boroboroton © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-noppera-bo-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Noppera-bo © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-rokurokubi-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Rokurokubi © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What he photographs: ghosts in flesh and blood. A head drifting away at the end of an endless neck, over a folding screen painted with mountains ( Rokurokubi ). A face as smooth as an egg, arms raised in a striped kimono ( Noppera-bō ). A woman swallowed by her own hair ( Kejōrō ). Two heads for a single body ( Dōmokōmo ). A tattered futon that takes on a life of its own ( Boroboroton ). And Miku (未来, “future”), a creature invented by Yuji Watanabe, whose features slide across the face like dripping wax. Miku, according to curator Charli Sas, “carries the tradition into the present.” The dread lies in a slight shift, like a frame hung crooked in a hotel room."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A risky bet, folklore staged by a fashion photographer? It depends: look at Irving Penn. Still, the danger has a name, costume, and Mendon , with its spiral headdress set on a straw skirt, comes close. Yuji Watanabe wards it off through material. The 8×10 Polaroid gives the bodies a velvety grain, deep blacks, frayed edges, the patina of an old print found at the bottom of a trunk. The film itself joins the world of ghosts."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-mendon-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Mendon © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-shibaten-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Shibaten © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-domokomo-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Domokomo © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/yokai-zan-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Zan © Yuji Watanabe", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Is there anybody there? The séance question is put, this time, to the landscapes. For this new series, Yuji Watanabe traveled across Japan with One Instant peel-apart film, a process in which the positive is separated from the negative by hand, leaving burns, streaks or yellow seams along the edges. Mountains, forests, caves, waterfalls, still waters. A cave turned violet. A sea of clouds as pink as a cheek. A field of snow in black and white. The frames remain empty, the tension rises. Charli Sas sums it up: “Some carry associations with death, demons, or otherworldly forces; others seem to reveal nothing.” Then, further on: “Yet once you have encountered the yōkai, that nothingness begins to feel inhabited.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "At Picto New York, the hanging takes the form of an emaki (絵巻), the Japanese illustrated handscroll unrolled with one hand and rolled up with the other, scene after scene. Yuji Watanabe had not planned it: the idea, the artist says, came later, when he was working out the exhibition space. article_text:
“A yōkai is a fallen god,” wrote Yanagita Kunio, the father of Japanese folklore studies. The line already accompanied Yuji Watanabe’s exhibition “Yōkai” at 229 Gallery in Tokyo in September 2024, and it opens every door. A god knocked off his pedestal, then, driven out of the shrines, taking refuge behind folding screens, in faded kimonos, under old futons. A harsh fall from grace. Sacred monsters, in the literal sense.

Yuji Watanabe knows the power of metamorphosis. Trained in Japan, he studied photography in New York, returned to Tokyo, then settled in Paris in 2012. He shoots fashion stories for international magazines, a world where a coat is enough to change a silhouette (creatures demand more). Alongside it grew a personal practice, analog and stubborn. As he explains, the fantastic needs the real in order to exist: without that share of reality at the moment of creation, he himself stops feeling the fantastic, hence his attachment to analog processes. The large-format camera, the light, the chemistry, all of it.

What he photographs: ghosts in flesh and blood. A head drifting away at the end of an endless neck, over a folding screen painted with mountains ( Rokurokubi ). A face as smooth as an egg, arms raised in a striped kimono ( Noppera-bō ). A woman swallowed by her own hair ( Kejōrō ). Two heads for a single body ( Dōmokōmo ). A tattered futon that takes on a life of its own ( Boroboroton ). And Miku (未来, “future”), a creature invented by Yuji Watanabe, whose features slide across the face like dripping wax. Miku, according to curator Charli Sas, “carries the tradition into the present.” The dread lies in a slight shift, like a frame hung crooked in a hotel room.

A risky bet, folklore staged by a fashion photographer? It depends: look at Irving Penn. Still, the danger has a name, costume, and Mendon , with its spiral headdress set on a straw skirt, comes close. Yuji Watanabe wards it off through material. The 8×10 Polaroid gives the bodies a velvety grain, deep blacks, frayed edges, the patina of an old print found at the bottom of a trunk. The film itself joins the world of ghosts.

Is there anybody there? The séance question is put, this time, to the landscapes. For this new series, Yuji Watanabe traveled across Japan with One Instant peel-apart film, a process in which the positive is separated from the negative by hand, leaving burns, streaks or yellow seams along the edges. Mountains, forests, caves, waterfalls, still waters. A cave turned violet. A sea of clouds as pink as a cheek. A field of snow in black and white. The frames remain empty, the tension rises. Charli Sas sums it up: “Some carry associations with death, demons, or otherworldly forces; others seem to reveal nothing.” Then, further on: “Yet once you have encountered the yōkai, that nothingness begins to feel inhabited.”

At Picto New York, the hanging takes the form of an emaki (絵巻), the Japanese illustrated handscroll unrolled with one hand and rolled up with the other, scene after scene. Yuji Watanabe had not planned it: the idea, the artist says, came later, when he was working out the exhibition space. A soundscape by Pinkcourtesyphone, the project of composer Richard Chartier, runs from one photograph to the next and extends the uncertainty beyond the image. The curator places the whole “somewhere between dream and nightmare.” Well measured.

Among the places photographed is Mount Osore, at the northern tip of Honshu, often described as a border between this world and the afterlife. Yuji Watanabe set down his camera there and left the frame empty, for the fallen gods to move in. “I took each and every photograph with a deep sense of gratitude.”

“Yōkai and Landscapes” by Yuji Watanabe is on view at Picto New York in Brooklyn through December 15, 2026.

article_text:
“ Clayface ,” a body-horror film based on a little-known comic book, opened to $24 million, a middling result for DC Studios, which is in year two of its mixed-bag theatrical revival.

On the one hand, the gross isn’t bad considering that the title character is a niche player and the gory genre isn’t associated with the spandex set. On the other, it’s slightly below projections, which predicted that “Clayface” would open to between $25 million to $30 million. It was enough to hold off the second weekend of A24’s “You Can See Everything,” which earned $19.5 million. It also helps that “Clayface” is cheaper than most comic book movies, carrying a price tag of $44 million. It may not be a profit-generating machine, but it won’t lose money either.

That wasn’t the case with “Supergirl,” the previous film in the universe that James Gunn and Peter Safran have been building since they took the reins at DC. “Supergirl” was a disaster, losing an estimated $80 million to $120 million . It also received a critical drubbing. “Clayface” fared better in that respect too. It stands at 75% “fresh” on Rotten Tomatoes compared to “Supergirl’s” 52% “rotten” rating. So far, last summer’s “Superman,” which Gunn wrote and directed, is the most successful example of their quippy, poppy approach. It earned $618.7 million globally and was widely embraced by critics. The company’s streaming shows, which include “Lanterns” and “Peacemaker,” have been better received.

But nothing DC has produced under Gunn and Safran has come close to the box office heights enjoyed by Christopher Nolan’s “The Dark Knight” trilogy, the first “Aquaman,” or “Wonder Woman.” Two of Nolan’s “Dark Knight” movies topped $1 billion, as did “Aquaman,” while “Wonder Woman” earned $823.9 million. When Gunn and Safran were enlisted to revitalize DC, the brand was struggling with consistency, with films like “Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom” and “The Flash” collapsing in spectacular fashion — they were little seen and little enjoyed. The product the pair has produced has improved on that low bar, even as DC’s more recent efforts have yet to deliver the same gloriously demented pleasures of Gunn’s “Guardians of the Galaxy” films. Safran, a veteran producer whose credits include “The Conjuring” franchise, is seen as the business brains of the operation, while Gunn speaks comic book and is tasked with charting the creative vision.

Looking ahead, DC will bring back some of its headliners. “The Batman: Part II” will open in theaters in 2028, while Gunn will return to the world of Superman with next summer’s “Man of Tomorrow.” Both films seem poised to connect with audiences.

Ultimately, Gunn and Safran may just have the misfortune of leading a comic book empire at a time when audiences are getting much more selective about their costumed heroes. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is the highest-grossing film of the year, having earned $2.5 billion, but that film features one of the most iconic comic book characters in history. Likewise, “Avengers: Doomsday” is expected to be a blockbuster when it opens in December, but it boasts Robert Downey Jr. and Chris Evans returning to the MCU. Outside of those Tiffany brands, even Marvel, which DC so clearly wants to emulate, has struggled. The company’s attempts to build up a new group of Avengers, such as “Thunderbolts,” “The Fantastic Four: First Steps,” “The Eternals,” and “The Marvels,” have been box office disappointments, if not outright bombs . If the king of comic book universes is struggling, maybe it’s wrong to hope for more from Gunn and Safran. In that kind of atmosphere, “Clayface” may count as a win, modest though its victory may be.
excerpt_original: James Gunn and Peter Safran were brought in to revitalize the comic book brand with mixed results.

title_original: Musei e uffici del MiC, il nodo Ales e il futuro di 2500 lavoratori della cultura
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "La data del 31 dicembre 2027 pesa sul futuro di oltre 2500 lavoratrici e lavoratori, impiegati nei musei, nei parchi archeologici, negli archivi, nelle biblioteche e negli uffici del Ministero della Cultura: è il termine fissato dall’attuale quadro normativo per l’utilizzo di Ales – Arte Lavoro e Servizi Spa , società in house del MiC che negli ultimi anni ha assunto un ruolo sempre più esteso nel funzionamento della rete culturale statale.", "links": [{"text": "Ales – Arte Lavoro e Servizi Spa", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/ales/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A lanciare nuovamente l’allarme sono Filcams Cgil, Fisascat Cisl e UilTucs, che chiedono al ministro della Cultura Alessandro Giuli la convocazione urgente di un tavolo istituzionale. Secondo i sindacati, il tempo a disposizione è ormai breve, perché per garantire continuità alla società e salvaguardare l’occupazione sarebbe necessario un intervento normativo. In assenza di risposte, le tre sigle hanno annunciato una campagna straordinaria di assemblee nei luoghi di lavoro, destinata a culminare in un’assemblea nazionale a Roma, senza escludere successive mobilitazioni."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Ales, perché il 31 dicembre 2027 è una data decisiva per i lavoratori della cultura"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il nodo deriva dall’articolo 1-ter del decreto-legge 104 del 2019, modificato negli anni successivi. La disposizione autorizza il Ministero della Cultura ad avvalersi di Ales per attività di accoglienza e vigilanza nei musei e nei parchi archeologici, oltre che per servizi di supporto tecnico, amministrativo e contabile, nelle more delle procedure concorsuali necessarie a soddisfare il fabbisogno di personale del dicastero e comunque non oltre il 31 dicembre 2027."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Tale formulazione lega il futuro di Ales al progressivo completamento degli organici ministeriali. In altre parole, la società è stata utilizzata anche come risposta alla cronica carenza di personale del MiC, mentre parallelamente lo Stato procedeva – con tempi spesso molto più lunghi – alle assunzioni tramite concorso."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Negli ultimi anni i diversi concorsi per funzionari, assistenti e altre figure professionali hanno effettivamente cercato di ricostituire gli organici del Ministero. Questo processo riduce almeno in parte il peso che Ales ha avuto negli anni più difficili della carenza di personale ma apre una questione occupazionale: più le strutture ministeriali vengono rifornite di personale pubblico, più diventa necessario definire quali funzioni debbano continuare a essere affidate alla partecipata e quale destino debbano avere le professionalità – in molti casi altamente specializzate – già impiegate."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Una società diventata strutturale per musei e uffici"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Fondata nel 1998, interamente partecipata dal Ministero della Cultura dal 2009 e attualmente guidata dal presidente e amministratore delegato Fabio Tagliaferri , Ales è cresciuta fino a diventare una delle strutture più rilevanti nel funzionamento operativo del sistema culturale statale. La legge le attribuisce attività di supporto alla conservazione e alla valorizzazione del patrimonio, all’accoglienza e alla vigilanza, oltre a funzioni tecnico-amministrative. Il Ministero può inoltre avvalersene per gli interventi connessi al PNRR, in questo caso fino alla conclusione del Piano e comunque entro il 31 dicembre 2026."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Secondo le organizzazioni sindacali, oggi Ales conta oltre 2.500 dipendenti. article_text:
La data del 31 dicembre 2027 pesa sul futuro di oltre 2500 lavoratrici e lavoratori, impiegati nei musei, nei parchi archeologici, negli archivi, nelle biblioteche e negli uffici del Ministero della Cultura: è il termine fissato dall’attuale quadro normativo per l’utilizzo di Ales – Arte Lavoro e Servizi Spa , società in house del MiC che negli ultimi anni ha assunto un ruolo sempre più esteso nel funzionamento della rete culturale statale.

A lanciare nuovamente l’allarme sono Filcams Cgil, Fisascat Cisl e UilTucs, che chiedono al ministro della Cultura Alessandro Giuli la convocazione urgente di un tavolo istituzionale. Secondo i sindacati, il tempo a disposizione è ormai breve, perché per garantire continuità alla società e salvaguardare l’occupazione sarebbe necessario un intervento normativo. In assenza di risposte, le tre sigle hanno annunciato una campagna straordinaria di assemblee nei luoghi di lavoro, destinata a culminare in un’assemblea nazionale a Roma, senza escludere successive mobilitazioni.

Ales, perché il 31 dicembre 2027 è una data decisiva per i lavoratori della cultura

Il nodo deriva dall’articolo 1-ter del decreto-legge 104 del 2019, modificato negli anni successivi. La disposizione autorizza il Ministero della Cultura ad avvalersi di Ales per attività di accoglienza e vigilanza nei musei e nei parchi archeologici, oltre che per servizi di supporto tecnico, amministrativo e contabile, nelle more delle procedure concorsuali necessarie a soddisfare il fabbisogno di personale del dicastero e comunque non oltre il 31 dicembre 2027.

Tale formulazione lega il futuro di Ales al progressivo completamento degli organici ministeriali. In altre parole, la società è stata utilizzata anche come risposta alla cronica carenza di personale del MiC, mentre parallelamente lo Stato procedeva – con tempi spesso molto più lunghi – alle assunzioni tramite concorso.

Negli ultimi anni i diversi concorsi per funzionari, assistenti e altre figure professionali hanno effettivamente cercato di ricostituire gli organici del Ministero. Questo processo riduce almeno in parte il peso che Ales ha avuto negli anni più difficili della carenza di personale ma apre una questione occupazionale: più le strutture ministeriali vengono rifornite di personale pubblico, più diventa necessario definire quali funzioni debbano continuare a essere affidate alla partecipata e quale destino debbano avere le professionalità – in molti casi altamente specializzate – già impiegate.

Una società diventata strutturale per musei e uffici

Fondata nel 1998, interamente partecipata dal Ministero della Cultura dal 2009 e attualmente guidata dal presidente e amministratore delegato Fabio Tagliaferri , Ales è cresciuta fino a diventare una delle strutture più rilevanti nel funzionamento operativo del sistema culturale statale. La legge le attribuisce attività di supporto alla conservazione e alla valorizzazione del patrimonio, all’accoglienza e alla vigilanza, oltre a funzioni tecnico-amministrative. Il Ministero può inoltre avvalersene per gli interventi connessi al PNRR, in questo caso fino alla conclusione del Piano e comunque entro il 31 dicembre 2026.

Secondo le organizzazioni sindacali, oggi Ales conta oltre 2.500 dipendenti. È una dimensione che rende difficile considerare la vicenda come una normale riorganizzazione aziendale: negli anni la società ha di fatto sostenuto una parte molto ampia della rete museale e degli uffici culturali italiani, compensando vuoti di organico che in alcuni casi incidevano direttamente sulla possibilità di garantire aperture, servizi al pubblico e attività amministrative.

Una cessazione improvvisa o una forte riduzione delle attività, senza un piano di transizione, potrebbe quindi produrre conseguenze sia sui posti di lavoro che sulla continuità di moltissimi servizi. Il rischio di una paralisi generalizzata va valutato alla luce del progressivo ingresso di nuovo personale ministeriale ma rimane evidente la necessità di capire quali attività oggi dipendano ancora concretamente dai lavoratori Ales e quali possano essere assorbite dagli organici pubblici.

Il confronto con l’azienda e le incognite sul futuro

Nell’incontro del 3 novembre, secondo quanto riferito dai sindacati, il management di Ales ha ribadito la solidità economica della società e la volontà di lavorare per superare il limite temporale previsto dalla normativa, anche individuando nuovi servizi specialistici da svolgere a supporto del Ministero. Non sono però emerse garanzie definitive sul futuro dell’azienda e dei suoi dipendenti.

Già nelle scorso settimane, UilTucs aveva richiamato l’attenzione sull’Atto di indirizzo del Ministero della Cultura del 25 agosto 2026, che contiene indicazioni su riorganizzazione, nuove attività, politiche del personale, formazione, riqualificazione, rapporti a tempo determinato e interventi collegati al PNRR. Il sindacato aveva però espresso dubbi sulle modalità concrete di applicazione, soprattutto rispetto alla possibile riallocazione del personale tra commesse e alla varietà delle professionalità presenti nella società.

Per Filcams, Fisascat e UilTucs la questione non può quindi essere risolta esclusivamente all’interno del rapporto tra management e lavoratori. La richiesta è che il confronto venga trasferito sul piano politico, perché l’eventuale prosecuzione delle attività oltre il 2027 richiede una scelta normativa. I sindacati chiedono che la discussione inizi ora. «Non chiediamo rassicurazioni generiche», affermano, ma un confronto istituzionale sul futuro della società e dell’occupazione.

Ales e l’ibridazione tra pubblico e privato nella cultura

La vicenda riapre anche una questione più generale sul modello con cui negli ultimi anni è stato organizzato il lavoro nel settore culturale pubblico. Pur essendo una società interamente controllata dal Ministero, Ales assume i propri dipendenti con contratti di natura privatistica e rappresenta forse l’esempio più evidente di quella zona di confine tra pubblico e privato che si è progressivamente ampliata anche nella gestione dei beni culturali italiani.

Il modello ha consentito al Ministero di reclutare personale con maggiore rapidità rispetto ai tempi dei concorsi pubblici e di rispondere a carenze diventate strutturali. Allo stesso tempo, però, ha prodotto una condizione più vulnerabile per migliaia di lavoratori che svolgono attività di interesse pubblico senza appartenere direttamente ai ruoli ministeriali.

A questa ambiguità si aggiunge un secondo problema, emerso più volte nell’organizzazione concreta del lavoro: il rapporto non sempre lineare tra competenze possedute, mansioni, inquadramenti e destinazioni operative. La flessibilità che ha reso Ales uno strumento utile per tamponare rapidamente le necessità del sistema può diventare, quando mutano le esigenze del Ministero, uno degli elementi di maggiore fragilità.

article_text:
Art Basel Paris wegen Unruhen möglicherweise nicht das ganze Wochenende geöffnet, Kulturkampf in Kolumbien – und gehypte Doku über Elizabeth Holmes kommt nach Deutschland: Das ist unsere Medienschau am Donnerstag

Kunstmarkt

Roxana Azimi berichtet in "Le Monde" , dass die Spannungen in der Stadt den Andrang internationaler Sammler auf die Art Basel Paris nicht gebremst hätten. Die Messe überzeuge mit hochkarätigen Entdeckungen und politisch aufgeladenen Werken, etwa von Steven Parrino und Anita Molinero. Galeristen wie Georges-Philippe Vallois zeigten sich erleichtert: "Ich hatte befürchtet, dass der Kontext die Käufer abschrecken würde, aber das war nicht der Fall." Nathalie Obadia meldete mehr als 20 Verkäufe am ersten Nachmittag, Iwan Wirth lobte die "Widerstandsfähigkeit des Marktes". Zugleich beobachtet Azimi eine zunehmende Polarisierung: Während die Kunstwelt unter dem Eindruck der Proteste feiere, riefen radikale Stimmen zur Besetzung des Grand Palais auf. Händler Christian Berst warnt vor den Folgen für ein ganzes Ökosystem, das vom Kunstmarkt lebe. Ob die Messe wie geplant bis Sonntag geöffnet bleibt, ist offen. Ist Kunst ein Vebraucherthema? Zumindest kann es das sein. Im Magazin "Marktplatz" des Deutschlandfunks, das sich sonst eher um Stromverträge und Lebensmittelqualität dreht, ging es am heutigen Donnerstag um den Kauf von Kunst . Wie sich Anfängerinnen und Anfänger an dieses Feld herantrauen können, erklärten dabei unter anderem der Galerist Kristian Jarmuschek und der Kunstkritiker Stefan Koldehoff. Fazit: Keine Berührungsängste haben, Institutionen wie Galerien und Kunstvereine besuchen, viel fragen und nur kaufen, was man auch wirklich mag. Das mit der Geldanlage funktioniert eh nur sehr selten und mit sehr viel Expertise. Der Kunstmarkt, so entfesselt er manchmal sein mag, birgt immer noch einen großen Teil Unsicherheit und Zufall.

Kulturpolitik

Patricia Hempel beschäftigt sich in der "Berliner Zeitung" eingehender mit Wolfram Weimers Warnung vor einer möglichen rot-grün-roten Landesregierung in Berlin . Der Kulturstaatsminister drohte mit "direkten Auswirkungen auf die schwarz-rote Kulturpolitik im Bund". Das Bundesfinanzministerium stellt jedoch klar, dass der Hauptstadtfinanzierungsvertrag über rund fünf Milliarden Euro für 2028 bis 2037 rechtsverbindlich ist und keine Kündigungsmöglichkeit enthält. Offen bleibt, ob Weimer Fördermittel außerhalb des Vertrags antasten könnte. Die Berliner Grünen weisen seine Drohungen zurück. Landeschef Philmon Ghirmai empfiehlt ihm, "vor der eigenen Haustüre zu kehren", und verweist auf mögliche Kooperationen von CDU und AfD. Hempel zeigt, dass die konkreten Folgen von Weimers Warnung bislang ungeklärt sind.

Kim Córdova berichtet in "Artnet News" über einen politischen Eingriff in das Museo Nacional de Colombia in Bogotá . Nach der Ausrufung eines "Kulturkampf" durch den neuen kolumbianischen Präsidenten Abelardo de la Espriella ließ die Regierung Dutzende Kunstwerke und historische Objekte entfernen, darunter Zeugnisse des Friedensprozesses von 2016 sowie Arbeiten zu LGBTQ-Rechten und indigenen Gemeinschaften. Die Künstlerin Doris Salcedo nennt das Vorgehen wie "aus einer Anleitung für Nazis". Kritiker sehen darin einen Angriff auf die kulturelle Vielfalt und die Verfassung, die den Schutz des kulturellen Erbes garantiert. Am Montag ordnete ein Richter an, weitere Ausstellungsänderungen auszusetzen. Córdova stellt den Vorgang in den Kontext von Budgetkürzungen und dem Abbau staatlicher Kulturförderung. Künstler und Wissenschaftler reagieren mit Protesten und öffentlichen Lehrveranstaltungen vor dem Museum.

Die besondere Doku

Die überraschend erfolgreiche Dokumentation über die inhaftierte Theranos-Gründerin Elizabeth Holmes kommt in deutsche Kinos. Der Film "You Can See Everything" von Nathan Fielder und Lance Oppenheim startet hierzulande am 3. Dezember, wie Sony Pictures bei Instagram mitteilte. Zuvor hatte es Spekulationen gegeben, ob und wann die gehypte Doku, die bereits unzählige Memes generiert hat, nach ihrem US-Kinostart auch nach Deutschland kommt. In den USA läuft der Film bereits seit Mitte Oktober. Am ersten Wochenende spielte er 15 Millionen US-Dollar in 855 Kinos ein, wie aus Zahlen des Branchenportals "Boxoffice Mojo" hervorgeht. Das sei der beste Dokumentarfilmstart in Nordamerika ohne Konzertfilme seit mehr als 20 Jahren, berichteten mehrere US-Medien übereinstimmend. Einige Medien sehen "You Can See Everything" bereits als Oscar-Anwärter. Die Kritiken fallen auffallend positiv aus. Auf den Plattformen IMDb und Letterboxd, wo Nutzerinnen und Nutzer selbst Bewertungen abgeben, gehört die Doku bislang zu den am besten bewerteten Filmen überhaupt. Holmes war Gründerin und Chefin des Start-ups Theranos, mit dem sie Bluttests zu revolutionieren versprach. Bei Theranos reichten angeblich nur wenige Tropfen Blut auch für komplexe Tests. Holmes wurde gefeiert, Theranos erreichte in Finanzierungsrunden eine Bewertung von neun Milliarden Dollar. Holmes wurde damit auf dem Papier zur Milliardärin. Doch dann stellte sich heraus, dass die Technologie nicht funktionierte. Holmes und ihr Top-Manager Ramesh Balwani wurden wegen des Vorwurfs verurteilt, Investoren gezielt hinters Licht geführt zu haben. Sie ging 2023 ins Gefängnis. Nach aktuellen Angaben der US-Gefängnisverwaltung soll sie Ende Februar 2030 entlassen werden. Die Doku beginnt einen Monat vor dem Haftantritt. Nach der Premiere auf einem Filmfestival in den USA und dem starken Kinostart wurde in sozialen Medien auch die Frage über einen Kinostart in Deutschland immer lauter. Da ein genauer Termin lange offen geblieben war, kündigten manche Nutzer gar an, eine Reise über die Grenze nach Polen zu planen – dort soll der Film bereits am 6. November in die Kinos kommen. Den deutschen Starttermin kündigten mehrere Kinoketten nun ebenfalls direkt in sozialen Medien an und stießen damit auf großen Anklang.

editorial_title_zh: 独立肖像：桑莱·索里（Sanlé Sory）镜头下的彩色国度
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在伦敦摄影师画廊（The Photographers’ Gallery），“桑莱·索里：彩色岁月”（Sanlé Sory: Colour Years）展现了这位布基纳法索摄影师职业生涯中鲜为人知的一章，记录了独立后布基纳法索不断变迁的身份认同、文化表达与日常生活。 19 october 2026 What […]

article_text:
At The Photographers’ Gallery in London, ‘Sanlé Sory: Colour Years’ reveals a lesser-known chapter in the Burkinabé photographer’s career, documenting changing identities, cultural expression and everyday life in post-independence Burkina Faso.

What can a portrait reveal about a society in transformation? In ‘Sanlé Sory: Colour Years’, The Photographers’ Gallery revisits the remarkable career of one of West Africa’s most prolific photographers, revealing how colour photography captured the evolving identities and aspirations of a generation.

Best known for his black-and-white portraits of Bobo-Dioulasso’s vibrant youth culture, Sanlé Sory began experimenting with colour photography in the mid-1980s at his Volta Photo studio.

The exhibition presents meticulously restored colour prints from his archive, alongside record covers featuring Volta Jazz, a band associated with Burkina Faso’s flourishing post-independence music scene.

From families and couples to traders and shopkeepers, Sory’s portraits document changing fashions, relationships, and everyday experiences in a society negotiating political transformation and cultural exchange.

Established in 1960, the year of Upper Volta’s independence, Volta Photo became a space where individuals could construct and express their identities in front of the camera.

Curated by Taous Dahmani, ‘Colour Years’ offers a perspective on Sory’s enduring photographic legacy, foregrounding the relationship between portraiture, self-representation and social change.

Through colour, fashion and personal expression, the exhibition celebrates the individuals who shaped the visual history of modern Burkina Faso.

This exhibition is on view at The Photographers’ Gallery in London until 21 February 2027.

article_text:
I n 2017, when Brett Morgen began work on his acclaimed 2022 David Bowie documentary, Moonage Daydream , he was given complete access to the late star’s entire, cavernous archive. “My eyes were immediately drawn to a stack of gleaming 35mm cans with the word ‘Stage’ written on them,” he remembers.

At first, the director – whose work also includes Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck and the Rolling Stones documentary Crossfire Hurricane – assumed the cans might contain some sort of footage shot around Bowie’s 1978 live album, Stage, recorded in mostly in Philadelphia. However, he soon realised they actually contained the holy grail of Bowie artefacts: footage of the legendary Earl’s Court shows later that year, which had remained unseen for almost 50 years. “Making Moonage Daydream, I had access to every filmed performance in existence of David Bowie,” he says, “but when I saw this one I knew this was without question the greatest filmed performance of his career.”

In 1978, Bowie had commissioned Just a Gigolo director David Hemmings to film two of the three sold-out summer shows at the venue – where the star was touring Low and “Heroes” – with a view to showing the film in theatres in lieu of a physical tour (he wouldn’t take the road again until 1983). However, the singer subsequently started making the Lodger album, moved to Switzerland, was reportedly unhappy with the film’s editing and the entire project was subsequently left behind. “He was moving on to other things at the speed of light,” Morgen explains. “So at that point I think the idea of looking backwards was distasteful to him.”

Before his death in 2016, though, Bowie had floated the idea of finally putting it out. In the new year it will debut in arenas – not cinemas – almost half a century after it was made. Morgen and team spent nearly 10 years readying it for 2027 as a multimedia experience. “It became something of an obsession,” he admits. “We spent over 1,000 hours colour-grading the footage, which I believe is some sort of record, but we really wanted it to look and feel like something you would experience today.”

It helped that the footage had been beautifully shot and perfectly preserved in Bowie’s storage unit, with excellent sound recorded by Bowie’s producer, Tony Visconti. Missing from Morgen’s film will be the extraneous stuff Hemmings added to the concerts. “I found a lot of footage of a young boy playing David that I was a bit confused by,” the director grins. “That’s not in the film.” Instead, it focuses on Bowie – in wonderfully billowing trousers and makeup – at the peak of his performance powers. “He looks amazing,” Morgen smiles. “I’ve looked at close-ups and I think: how on earth is this man not sweating?”

By the time the Isolar II tour reached Earl’s Court, Bowie and band were at the pinnacle of their game, signposting the future. “To have an electric violin, a piano and a synth player in a rock show in 1978 was extraordinary,” says Morgen, whose film combines songs from both nights because “It was very improvisational. Different arrangements two nights running. You can feel the danger and excitement that it could have gone off the rails at any moment and David was very charged by that.

“The audacity of starting the show with Warszawa, perhaps the lowest-energy first song of any rock concert ever – but that’s Bowie. By the end of the first set he’s reeled them in and by the end of the second set the place is just insane. The performance of Station to Station is incredible.”

During the second show, on 1 July, Bowie quips, “OK, this will be interesting”, and performs Sound and Vision for the first time ever. “And he’s cracking up throughout the song because I think the electric violin was trying to do the horn section, which David thought was kind of amusing. It’s a great moment. Then the camera stays with David when he goes off to the sides, having a glass of beer or smoking a cigarette, and he’s so engaged, dancing and smiling. It’s very joyous. I think this was the first time he’d performed without a mask, or ‘character’, so to speak.”

Morgen isn’t giving everything away but promises “surprises” as well as “a new medium of entertainment”.

“It’s not a movie that’s being shown in arenas,” he insists. “There’s multiple screens, a fully integrated lighting package, a 7.1 [surround sound] sound mix. The performance is 1978 but the presentation is 2027. The audience is invited to gaze where they want to gaze: choose your own adventure. Eleven years after his passing, it makes perfect sense that Bowie will be trailblazing again.”

article_text:
In a rare move, Mexico’s exhibition-distribution giant Cinépolis has landed Latin American rights to Spanish buzz title “5 More Minutes” (“5 Minutos Más”) starring Javier Cámara , who took home the Best Supporting Actor prize at the San Sebastian Film Festival.

“We normally pick up only Mexican rights to films about 90% of the time but we see this as a high concept genre film that has the potential to travel exceptionally well,” said Miguel Rivera, Cinépolis VP of global programming and content, who sat down with Variety at the Morelia Film Festival alongside his theatrical distribution senior manager Karla Marti and creative executive Francisca Barraza. According to Barraza, Cinépolis is casting its net wide to work with both established and budding talent. “We’re looking for fresh, original films across various genres,” Rivera added.

The company plans to release Javier Ruiz Caldera’s time-warping thriller, written and starring Berto Romero, on Jan. 28 next year, which it hopes will be an exceptional time for Mexican cinema. Cinépolis aims to increase its slate of Mexican pics to 12 a year, boarding some at their development phase. Overall attendance has grown at a healthy clip, but not for homegrown pics, which are capturing a mere 3% to 4% market share compared to an average 10% share in pre-pandemic years.

Cinépolis has three films playing during Morelia, including opening night film “Campeón Gabacho” by Jonas Cuarón, which it plans to release across 600 screens in Mexico aside from Central America.

In terms of box office results, this year has been the second best since the COVID slump although it has not quite reached its 2013 peak, bolstered by the phenomenal success of “The Super Mario Brothers Movie,” “Barbie” and “Oppenheimer,” said Rivera.

On Nov. 26, it releases Colombian Andrés Beltrán’s “El diablo sabe tu nombre” (translated to “The Devil Knows Your Name”) about a documentary filmmaking couple who risk their lives investigating an alleged possession and exorcism case.

Also revving its genre slate in April is the latest from “Km. 31” director Rigoberto Castañeda. Titled “Return to Me” (“Regresa”), it follows a grieving mother who, after the loss of her son, visits a remote Mexican village where she comes upon a cult on sacred Rarámuri land that claims it can bring her son back from the dead.

“While people have returned to cinemas for Hollywood blockbusters, it’s been harder to bring them back for local productions. So, we’re working hard to rebuild that audience and keep Mexican cinema growing,” said Cinépolis CEO, Alejandro Ramirez.

“The number of Mexican film titles has rebounded, but box office revenues haven’t followed. The pandemic changed viewing habits: audiences have grown accustomed to watching Mexican films, especially comedies, on streaming platforms rather than in theaters,” he observed.

Cinépolis is steadily recovering from the devastating impact of COVID-19, which forced it to close cinemas and permanently give up some locations.

“We’re opening new screens every year now, but we are being more selective, cherry picking so to speak. At the moment, we’re opening around 60 or 70 screens worldwide each year, which is much less than before the pandemic when we’d open an average of 300 screens a year,” said Ramirez.

According to 2025 statistics sourced from Cinépolis and other exhibitors, AMC reigns worldwide in terms of screen count, with 9,640, followed by China’s Wanda, with 8,743 and Cinepolis, 6,853.

“We’re on track to sell more tickets than any other cinema circuit in the world. While we don’t have the largest number of screens, we lead in ticket sales and have the highest attendance per screen globally,” Ramirez pointed out.

The same statistics show Cinépolis reporting 256.4 million admissions in 2025 compared to AMC’s 219.4 million and Wanda’s 212.8 million.

In terms of admissions per screen worldwide, Cinépolis leads with 37,417 compared to AMC’s 22,761 and Wanda’s 25,117.

With new cinemas in the pipeline through 2029, the company remains optimistic about the industry’s future. “If cinema survived a two-year global pandemic, I don’t think it’s going anywhere,” Ramirez said. “It was the ultimate stress test, and we’ve come through it. Let’s just hope there are no more pandemics.”

Last September, Ramirez participated in the inaugural Lumière Summit, presided over by France’s President Emmanuel Macron and his South Korean counterpart Lee Jae Myung.

“It was refreshing to see France and South Korea give cinema and the communal big-screen experience such prominence at the highest level of government,” he said. Inspired by France’s My Class at the Cinema program, which takes 2.5 million children and teenagers to cinemas annually, he highlighted the importance of cultivating new audiences.

Following a meeting with President Macron, Cinépolis signed an agreement with Unifrance to expand the French Film Tour—which began in Mexico 30 years ago and has reached 49.5 million moviegoers across 90 cities—to Spain, India, Indonesia and Chile in 2027. “We also want to replicate France’s success in visual literacy and audience development, while bringing more Mexican cinema to international markets, including Europe.”

The Morelia Film Festival opened on Oct. 16 and wraps Oct. 25.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios has entered production on its Kevin Bacon horror film Summoner , with two additions to the cast: Daniel Ings ( The Gentlemen ) and Stephanie Beatriz ( A Man on the Inside ).

No word on roles played by the duo.

Written and directed by Jeremy Slater, the film follows Jefferson Haddock (Bacon), who is called into an isolated witness protection property to deal with a terrifying demon, unleashing a force that threatens to end him and everything around him.

Related Stories

Top 50 Classic Horror Movies

Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’

Summoner ‘s cast also includes the previously announced Giorgia Whigham. Andy Muschietti, Barbara Muschietti, and Russell Ackerman are producing alongside executive producers Dan Kagan, Melissa Russell, Carl Hampe, and John Schoenfelder. The film will be released in theaters at a date not yet disclosed.

Watch on Deadline

A British actor best known for his work on shows like Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen and HBO’s Game of Thrones prequel A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , Ings can currently be seen starring opposite Catherine Zeta-Jones in Prime Video’s Kill Jackie . He has a stacked slate coming up, including Shawn Levy’s Star Wars: Starfighter , the Cynthia Erivo legal drama Prima Facie recently launched out of TIFF, and David Leitch’s Jason Statham Stole My Bike — plus Apple dramedy The Husbands opposite Juno Temple and the Channel 4 series The Rachel Incident . He is repped by United Agents, WME, ColorCreative, TFC Management, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

Best known for starring opposite Andy Samberg in the Fox comedy Brooklyn Nine-Nine , Beatriz’s recent credits include A Man on the Inside and Don’t Say Good Luck for Netflix, as well as such animated series as The Legend of Vox Machina , Krapopolis and Hazbin Hotel . She is repped by Gersh, Authentic, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman.

article_text:
100年間、博物館に眠っていた化石が「新種の肉食恐竜」と判明──ヨーロッパ初のメガラプトル類か

博物館で長らく見過ごされていた 化石 が、新種の 恐竜 のものであることが最新の研究で明らかになった。100年以上前に イギリス ・ワイト島でアマチュアの化石ハンターが採集した骨の断片を新たに調べたところ、長い爪が特徴の肉食恐竜メガラプトル類に属する新種であることが判明している。

イギリス ・ ロンドン のサウスケンジントンにある自然史博物館には、数百万点もの標本が収蔵されている。その中から、同館に存在していることすら知られていなかった 恐竜 の標本が最近見つかった。

それは、およそ1世紀にわたり同博物館が保管していた頭骨の断片で、最新技術を用いた研究によって新種の恐竜のものであることが判明したと科学雑誌ディスカバーが伝えている。さらに注目すべきは、ヨーロッパで初めて確認されたメガラプトル類である可能性が高いという点だ。肉食恐竜のメガラプトル類は、これまで欧州以外の地域からは見つかっている。

イギリス南部のワイト島でこの 化石 を発見したのは、アマチュア化石ハンターのレジナルド・ウォルター・トゥーリーだ。トゥーリーが1924年に死去した後、自然史博物館は彼が採集したものから1000点以上の標本を取得。その中には今回研究対象となった頭骨の断片の化石も含まれており、のちに恐竜のものであると特定されたが種類は不明のままだった。

しかし、研究者たちがその古い骨を詳しく調べたところ、新種恐竜の同定という驚くべき新展開につながった。CTスキャンで頭骨の3次元モデルを作成して内部構造を解析し、これまで難しかった解剖学的特徴の詳細な確認ができるようになったからだ。研究では頭骨の後部にあたるこの断片を他の肉食恐竜の頭骨と比較し、複数の特徴の組み合わせからメガラプトル類の新種と判断した。

「インヴィクティベラトリックス・アンベリナ（Invictibellatrix amberina）」と命名されたこの新種恐竜に関する研究成果は、10月14日にロイヤル・ソサエティ・オープン・サイエンス誌（Royal Society Open Science）で 発表 されている。

優雅にも思えるその名前とは裏腹に、メガラプトル類は長く鋭い爪を持つ肉食恐竜の一群で、ティラノサウルスの近縁であるとする説もある。しかし、その捕食方法には大きな違いがあり、ティラノサウルスのように巨大な顎で噛みつくのではなく、鋭い爪のついた力強い腕を獲物の捕獲に利用していたと考えられる。

生息時期は約1億2000万年前の白亜紀前期で、全長3〜4メートル、体高は約1.5メートルと見られる。羽毛が生えていた可能性もあるが、どんな外見だったかについては、今後の科学的な復元作業に委ねられている。

今回の研究成果にはまた、単なる新種発見以上の意義がある。メガラプトル類は アジア 、 オーストラリア 、南米で出土しているが、これまでヨーロッパでの確認例はなく、メガラプトル類が世界各地へどのように広がっていったのか、その分布がどう変化したかを研究する際の問題となっていた。

一説によると、メガラプトル類はアジアを起源とし、ヨーロッパを経由して西へ移動した後、最終的にかつて存在したゴンドワナ大陸──現在の南米、アフリカ、南極大陸、オーストラリアを含む──に到達したと考えられている。ワイト島で発見されたメガラプトル類の化石はこの説を裏付け、先史時代のイギリスの恐竜相が従来の推測より多様であったことを示唆するものだ。

研究論文の筆頭著者で、ユニバーシティ・カレッジ・ロンドンの研究者でもあるカシアス・モリソンは、長らく見過ごされてきたこの化石について、博物館の収蔵品にはまだまだ多くの発見の可能性が眠っていることを示す好例だと述べている。（翻訳：石井佳子）

title_original: European Film Academy unveils shortlist for 2027 European Film Awards
editorial_title_zh: 欧洲电影学院公布2027年欧洲电影奖短名单
editorial_excerpt_zh: 短名单包括《峡湾》、《未知女性》、《黄信》、《温柔的关爱》和《黑球》等电影节获奖作品。

"text": "欧洲电影学院已为2027年欧洲电影奖的可能提名作品公布了68部长片短名单，该奖项将于1月16日在雅典举行。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "短名单包括来自40个国家的45部剧情片、15部纪录片和8部动画长片。其中25部影片由女性导演或联合执导。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "滚动查看完整短名单", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "剧情片短名单包括备受瞩目的电影节作品，如克里蒂安·蒙吉的戛纳金棕榈奖得主《峡湾》、迈·埃尔·图基的威尼斯金狮奖得主《未知女性》、伊尔克·恰塔克的柏林金熊奖得主《黄信》以及哈维尔·卡沃和哈维尔·安布罗斯的多伦多观众奖得主《黑球》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其他入选的电影节获奖作品包括迈克·李的圣塞巴斯蒂安金壳奖得主《温柔的关爱》、弗洛林·谢尔班的洛迦诺金豹奖得主《你不属于这里》以及维萨尔·莫里纳的圣丹斯世界剧情片单元奖得主《羞耻与金钱》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，短名单还包括一系列电影节热门作品，如波兰导演帕维尔·帕利科夫斯基的《祖国》，该片与《黑球》共同获得戛纳最佳导演奖，以及西蒙·斯通的《埃尔西诺》，该片刚刚在伦敦电影节上首映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "来自戛纳的影片包括佩德罗·阿莫多瓦的《苦涩的圣诞节》，安德烈·兹瓦金采夫的《迷宫》，卢卡斯·东特的《胆小鬼》以及阿诺·博德里的两部曲《戴高乐传记》。威尼斯影片包括弗洛里安·泽勒的《地堡》和沃纳·赫尔佐格的《疯狂的快马》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纪录片短名单涵盖从威尼斯评审团奖得主尤瓦尔·亚伯拉罕与拉切尔·索尔的《纳扎》到戛纳纪录片奖得主佩加赫·阿哈南里的《革命排练》以及桑迪斯国际纪录片奖得主比利亚娜·图托罗夫与彼得·格洛马齐奇的《紧握一座山》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "动画短名单包括安纳西观众奖和评审团奖得主路易斯·克利奇的《铁男孩》以及戛纳首映的马克罗·阮与尼古拉斯·阿塔内的《吉姆女王》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "入选的剧情片和纪录片由欧洲电影学院董事会成员和特邀的欧洲专家选出，而入选的动画长片则由学院董事会成员和与动画协会（Cartoon，欧洲动画电影协会）合作的特邀专家组成的遴选委员会选出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "短名单的公布是EFA颁奖程序的第一步。在接下来的几周内，欧洲电影学院的5700名成员将观看入选影片并投票选出提名，除了欧洲发现奖（Prix Fipresci）、欧洲短片奖、欧洲年轻观众奖、LUX观众奖和荣誉奖项，这些奖项有单独的评选程序", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Source: Tudor Panduru

‘Fjord’

The European Film Academy has shortlisted 68 feature-length films for a possible nomination for the European Film Awards, which take place on January 16 in Athens.

The shortlist comprises 45 feature films, 15 documentary films and eight animated feature films from 40 countries. 25 film of the films are directed or co-directed by women.

Scroll down for full shortlist

The feature film shortlist includes high-profile festival titles such as Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord , Venice Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown by May el-Toukhy, Berlinale Golden Bear winner Yellow Letters by İlker Çatak and Toronto audience prize winner La Bola Negra by Javier Calvo & Javier Ambrossi.

Other festival victors shortlisted include San Sebastian Golden Shell winner Tender Loving Care by Mike Leigh, Florin Şerban’s Locarno Golden Leopard winner You Don’t Belong Here and Sundance world dramatic cinema winner Shame And Money by Visar Morina.

Elsewhere, the shortlist brings together an array of festival favourites, spanning Fatherland by Pawel Pawlikowski, which shared the Cannes best director prize with La Bola Negra, and Simon Stone’s Elsinore which just opened the BFI London Film Festival.

From Cannes, Pedro Almodóvar’s Bitter Christmas is on the shortlist, as is Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur, Lukas Dhont’s Coward and Antonin Baudry’s two-part De Gaulle biopic. Venice titles include Florian Zeller’s Bunker and Werner Herzog’s Bucking Fastard.

The documentary shortlist spans Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor’s NAZA , winner of the jury prize at Venice through to Pegah Ahangarani’s Rehearsals For A Revolution , winner of the Cannes documentary award and Biljana Tutorov & Petar Glomazić ’s To Hold A Mountain, winner of the Sundance international documentary prize.

The animation shortlist includes Annecy audience and jury prize winner Iron Boy by Louis Clichy and Cannes premiere Jim Queen by Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané.

The shortlisted feature and documentary films have been chosen by members of the European Film Academy board and invited European experts, while the shortlisted animated feature films were chosen by a selection committee composed of members of the Academy Board and invited experts in cooperation with Cartoon, the European Association of Animation Film.

The shortlist announcement is the first step in EFA’s awarding procedure. In the coming weeks, the 5,700 members of the European Film Academy will watch the shortlisted films and vote for the nominations, except for the European discovery – Prix Fipresci, European short film, European young audience award, LUX audience award and honorary awards, which have separate selection procedures

The nominations for key categories will be announced on November 14 during the Thessaloniki International Film Festival, while the European young audience award nominations will be announced on November 1 at the International Film Festival Glasgow. The short film nominations will be revealed at the Seville European Film Festival on November 13 The nominees for the LUX audience award will be unveiled on 25 November.

"而除了画作本身，最令人久久凝视的还有画框。黑底上施以金色装饰、带有立体雕刻的意匠让人感受到工匠的技艺。不仅是画师的笔墨，连衬托作品的画框都倾注了如此心血。在为其美感感到惊叹的同时，也不禁让人浮想联翩：当初奉纳的人们怀着怎样的想法，寄托了怎样的祈愿呢？在雕刻绘马中，还能欣赏到与绘画截然不同的立体表现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "paragraph", "text": "我们固然可以通过照片了解作品的面貌。但是，这种尺寸感、金色的光芒以及雕刻的深邃感，唯有亲临实物面前方能体会到吧。在公开期间，绘马堂内禁止拍照。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "负责策划制作的株式会社一旗代表董事东山武明也表示，大型绘马的尺寸感、立体感以及画框的造型，仅凭照片是很难完全传达的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "堂内还介绍了大型绘马的修复工序。根据展示资料，逸见（狩野）一信绘制的《五条橋の牛若丸と弁慶》（ 1847 年）目前正在修复中，可以通过照片了解作业的情况。我们同样希望关注这些将作品传承至下一个时代的手工劳作。此外，绘马堂内配有可用智能手机收听的语音导览，可自备耳机进行体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "实物公开寺宝画卷", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "寺宝《浅草寺寛文縁起絵巻》的实物展示也是一大看点。在宽文 2 年（ 1662 年）由狩野氏信绘制的全 6 卷中，第 1 卷描绘了兄弟二人捕鱼时网到观音像等浅草寺的创建传说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/155487bca38b7119f282a30de1635b0d.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "据认为是狩野氏信所绘《浅草寺寛文縁起絵巻》第1卷，宽文2年（1662），浅草寺藏。传递浅草寺创建相关场景的实物展示", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据东山代表介绍，去年展出的是复制品，而今年将公开实物。此外，还可以近距离欣赏国宝《法华经（开结共）》中相当于“观音经”部分的精美复制品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "大型绘马跃动、观音菩萨现身的本堂", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从宝蔵门走向本堂，这一次广阔的屋顶上将满眼呈现影像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "东山代表解释说，他们注重的并非单纯展示华丽的影像，而是将浅草寺特有的历史与藏品融入影像之中。除了以大型绘马和浅草寺相关的浮世绘为题材外，因战灾而烧毁的旧本堂栏间雕刻，也根据留存的照片通过影像进行了立体还原。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以大型绘马为题材的图象动态展开，接连呈现。令人联想到莲花的追光图案也分外美丽，让人忍不住发出“哇”的惊叹。观音菩萨等与浅草寺信仰相关的神佛形象也纷纷登场。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "白天在绘马堂凝视细节，夜晚抬头仰望以本堂大屋顶为舞台的影像。能够从不同的距离接触相同的浅草寺美术与历史，这让人觉得十分有趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "在传法院庭园中铺展的云海与光影", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在国家名胜·传法院庭园中，可以欣赏到人造云海与夜间灯光秀。东山代表也将伴随着云海同时眺望浅草寺五重塔与东京晴空塔的景色，列为本次的一大看点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "云海彼端排列着的五重塔与东京晴空塔。让人深切感受到古老与崭新，皆已融入这条街道的风景之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/9c550f2f8255fcc1ec02006f5adc8f71.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "国家名胜·传法院庭园的云海布景。将浅草寺五重塔与东京晴空塔尽收于同一景致中", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在绘马堂，可以近距离观赏画师与工匠的技艺。在夜晚的本堂，浅草寺的美术与历史伴随着光影延展开来。正是因为先看过了作品的细节，才会对影像中浮现的图象自然而然地投去目光。（撰稿人：森香织）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "※ 照片拍摄于 10 月 29 分钟不同的影像。免费、无需事前预约。传法院庭园与绘马堂特别参拜： 9 时～ 21 时。绘马堂开放至 16 时（最终入场 15 时 30 分），传法院庭园最终入场 20 时 30 分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "特别参拜当日票价：成人（高中生及以上） 2,500 日元，中小学生 1,000 日元。学龄前儿童免费。", "本堂の大屋根に映し出された、江戸時代の「朝比奈の大人形」を描いたとみられる図柄。浅草寺本堂へのプロジェクションマッピングは今回が初めて", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大絵馬を間近で鑑賞し、夜には浅草寺ゆかりの美術が巨大な屋根いっぱいに躍動する。浅草寺（東京都台東区）で 10 月 30 日から 11 月 3 日まで開催される「 ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026 」では、本堂と宝蔵門のプロジェクションマッピングに加え、通常非公開の絵馬堂や名勝・伝法院庭園を特別拝観できます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "今年は本堂にもプロジェクションマッピング"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "宝蔵門では、和の妖艶さを感じさせる色彩と光の中に、門を守る仁王像や、雷門にゆかりのある風神・雷神が現れます。目の前へ飛び出してくるかのような立体感と、映像に重なる音に引き込まれます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "text": "その先の本堂は、巨大で広々とした屋根が舞台。浅草寺ゆかりの絵画や仏教美術を題材にした映像が、レーザーやムービングライトとともに広がります。映像のもとになった美術を実物で見られるのが、絵馬堂の特別公開です。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "大絵馬に宿る、絵師と職人の技"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "普段は入れない絵馬堂には、歌川国芳や長谷川雪旦、逸見（狩野）一信らが描いたものを含む約 50 点の大絵馬が収蔵されています。階段から見渡すと、大きな額が壁に沿って並んでいます。大絵馬の前に立つと、まずその大きさに驚きます。けれど、近くで見る楽しさは、それだけではありません。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0f5030d6305c79cb0406a42616f9b496.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "通常非公開の浅草寺絵馬堂。階段の両側に大絵馬が並び、作品の大きさと展示空間の広がりが分かる", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "絵馬はもともと、神仏への祈りや感謝を込めて馬を奉納する習わしに由来するとされ、やがて人物や物語、花鳥などへ画題が広がりました。江戸時代には願主の依頼を受けた絵師たちも腕を振るい、その絵馬は多くの参詣者の目に触れる本堂などに掲げられました。祈りの場は、絵師たちが技を披露する場でもあったのです。《花卉に雉子》のような花鳥画もあり、題材の幅広さを感じます。"}, {"type": "image", "alt": "", "caption": "長谷川雪旦筆《錣引》（部分アップ）、天保11年（1840）、浅草寺所蔵。甲冑の細かな装飾が際立つ。", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "歌川国芳の《一ツ家》（ 1855 "paragraph", "text": "そして、絵と同じくらい見入ってしまったのが額縁です。黒地に金色の装飾が施され、立体的に彫り込まれた意匠には職人の技を感じます。絵師の筆だけでなく、作品を引き立てる額縁にも、これほど手がかけられている。その美しさに驚くと同時に、奉納した人々は何を思い、どんな祈りを込めたのだろうと想像が膨らみました。彫刻絵馬では、絵画とはまた異なる立体的な表現も楽しめます。"}, {"type": "image", "paragraph", "text": "写真で作品の姿を知ることはできます。でも、この大きさや金色の輝き、彫りの奥行きは、実物を前にしてこそ感じられるものではないでしょうか。一般公開中、絵馬堂内は撮影できません。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": 年）は修復中で、作業の様子を写真で知ることができます。作品を次の時代へ伝えるための手仕事にも目を向けたいところです。また、絵馬堂内にはスマートフォンで利用できる音声ガイドがあり、イヤホンを持参して楽しめます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "寺宝の絵巻を実物で公開"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "寺宝《浅草寺寛文縁起絵巻》の実物展示も見どころです。寛文 2 年（ 1662 年）、狩野氏信が描いたとされる全 6 巻のうち、第 1 巻には漁をしていた兄弟の網に観音像がかかったという浅草寺の創建伝承などが描かれています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東山代表によると、昨年は複製でしたが、今年は実物を公開。また、国宝《法華経（開結共）》のうち「観音経」にあたる部分の精巧な複製も、間近で鑑賞できます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "大絵馬が躍動し、観音菩薩も現れる本堂"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東山代表は、単に華やかな映像を見せるのではなく、浅草寺ならではの歴史や所蔵作品を映像に生かすことを大切にしたと説明します。大絵馬や浅草寺ゆかりの浮世絵を題材にするほか、戦災で失われた旧本堂の欄間彫刻も、残された写真をもとに映像で立体的に再現したといいます。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大絵馬を題材にした図像がダイナミックに動き出し、次々と現れる。蓮の花を思わせる光の模様も美しく、思わず「わぁ」と声が漏れました。観音菩薩など、浅草寺の信仰にゆかりのある仏の姿も登場します。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
大絵馬を間近で鑑賞し、夜には浅草寺ゆかりの美術が巨大な屋根いっぱいに躍動する。浅草寺（東京都台東区）で 10 月 30 日から 11 月 3 日まで開催される「 ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026 」では、本堂と宝蔵門のプロジェクションマッピングに加え、通常非公開の絵馬堂や名勝・伝法院庭園を特別拝観できます。

今年は本堂にもプロジェクションマッピング

昨年の宝蔵門に続き、今年は本堂でも初めてプロジェクションマッピングを実施。両会場で異なる約 6 分間の映像を、各日 18 時から 21 時 30 分まで交互に投影します。会場内ではスタッフの案内に従い、一方通行で鑑賞します。

宝蔵門では、和の妖艶さを感じさせる色彩と光の中に、門を守る仁王像や、雷門にゆかりのある風神・雷神が現れます。目の前へ飛び出してくるかのような立体感と、映像に重なる音に引き込まれます。

その先の本堂は、巨大で広々とした屋根が舞台。浅草寺ゆかりの絵画や仏教美術を題材にした映像が、レーザーやムービングライトとともに広がります。映像のもとになった美術を実物で見られるのが、絵馬堂の特別公開です。

大絵馬に宿る、絵師と職人の技

普段は入れない絵馬堂には、歌川国芳や長谷川雪旦、逸見（狩野）一信らが描いたものを含む約 50 点の大絵馬が収蔵されています。階段から見渡すと、大きな額が壁に沿って並んでいます。大絵馬の前に立つと、まずその大きさに驚きます。けれど、近くで見る楽しさは、それだけではありません。

絵馬はもともと、神仏への祈りや感謝を込めて馬を奉納する習わしに由来するとされ、やがて人物や物語、花鳥などへ画題が広がりました。江戸時代には願主の依頼を受けた絵師たちも腕を振るい、その絵馬は多くの参詣者の目に触れる本堂などに掲げられました。祈りの場は、絵師たちが技を披露する場でもあったのです。《花卉に雉子》のような花鳥画もあり、題材の幅広さを感じます。

長谷川雪旦の《楠公桜井の別れ》（ 1839 年）は、楠木正成と息子・正行の別れを描いた作品。金色の画面に甲冑の模様や装束の色が映え、近づくほど細かな描き込みに気付きます。

同じく雪旦の《錣引》（ 1840 年）では、組み合う武者たちの力強さに加え、兜や鎧の細部に目が留まりました。

歌川国芳の《一ツ家》（ 1855 年）は、同年の浅草寺の観音開帳に合わせて奉納された台東区指定有形文化財。浅草に伝わる物語を題材に、鉈を構える老婆とその娘、稚児に姿を変えた観音菩薩を描きます。緊迫した母娘の姿とは対照的に、観音菩薩は静かに座っています。額を含めた幅は約 3.6 メートル。その大きさにも圧倒されます。

そして、絵と同じくらい見入ってしまったのが額縁です。黒地に金色の装飾が施され、立体的に彫り込まれた意匠には職人の技を感じます。絵師の筆だけでなく、作品を引き立てる額縁にも、これほど手がかけられている。その美しさに驚くと同時に、奉納した人々は何を思い、どんな祈りを込めたのだろうと想像が膨らみました。彫刻絵馬では、絵画とはまた異なる立体的な表現も楽しめます。

写真で作品の姿を知ることはできます。でも、この大きさや金色の輝き、彫りの奥行きは、実物を前にしてこそ感じられるものではないでしょうか。一般公開中、絵馬堂内は撮影できません。

企画制作を手がける株式会社一旗の東山武明代表取締役も、大絵馬の大きさや立体感、額縁の造形は写真だけでは伝わりにくいと話していました。

堂内では大絵馬の修復工程も紹介されています。展示された資料によると、逸見（狩野）一信が描いた《五条橋の牛若丸と弁慶》（ 1847 年）は修復中で、作業の様子を写真で知ることができます。作品を次の時代へ伝えるための手仕事にも目を向けたいところです。また、絵馬堂内にはスマートフォンで利用できる音声ガイドがあり、イヤホンを持参して楽しめます。

寺宝の絵巻を実物で公開

寺宝《浅草寺寛文縁起絵巻》の実物展示も見どころです。寛文 2 年（ 1662 年）、狩野氏信が描いたとされる全 6 巻のうち、第 1 巻には漁をしていた兄弟の網に観音像がかかったという浅草寺の創建伝承などが描かれています。

東山代表によると、昨年は複製でしたが、今年は実物を公開。また、国宝《法華経（開結共）》のうち「観音経」にあたる部分の精巧な複製も、間近で鑑賞できます。

大絵馬が躍動し、観音菩薩も現れる本堂

宝蔵門から本堂へ進むと、今度は広い屋根いっぱいに映像が映し出されます。

東山代表は、単に華やかな映像を見せるのではなく、浅草寺ならではの歴史や所蔵作品を映像に生かすことを大切にしたと説明します。大絵馬や浅草寺ゆかりの浮世絵を題材にするほか、戦災で失われた旧本堂の欄間彫刻も、残された写真をもとに映像で立体的に再現したといいます。

大絵馬を題材にした図像がダイナミックに動き出し、次々と現れる。蓮の花を思わせる光の模様も美しく、思わず「わぁ」と声が漏れました。観音菩薩など、浅草寺の信仰にゆかりのある仏の姿も登場します。

昼は絵馬堂で細部を見つめ、夜は本堂の大屋根を舞台にした映像を見上げる。同じ浅草寺の美術や歴史に、異なる距離から触れられるのが面白いと感じました。

伝法院庭園に広がる雲海と光

国の名勝・伝法院庭園では、人工の雲海や夜間のライトアップが楽しめます。東山代表も、雲海とともに浅草寺の五重塔と東京スカイツリーを一緒に望める眺めを、見どころに挙げています。

雲海の向こうに並ぶ五重塔と東京スカイツリー。古いものも新しいものも、この街の景色になっているのだと感じます。

絵馬堂では、絵師と職人の技を間近に見ることができます。夜の本堂では、浅草寺の美術や歴史が光とともに広がります。作品の細部を見た後だからこそ、映像に現れる図像にも自然と目が向きました。（ライター・森 香織）

※ 写真は 10 月 29 日の内覧会で撮影したものです。一般公開中、絵馬堂内の撮影は禁止されています。

ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026

会場：浅草寺（東京都台東区浅草 2-3-1 ）

会期： 2026 年 10 月 30 日（金）～ 11 月 3 日（火・祝）

プロジェクションマッピング： 18 時～ 21 時 30 分。宝蔵門・本堂で異なる約 6 分間の映像を交互に投影。無料・事前申込不要。 伝法院庭園・絵馬堂の特別拝観： 9 時～ 21 時。絵馬堂は 16 時まで（最終入場 15 時 30 分）、伝法院庭園は最終入場 20 時 30 分。

特別拝観当日料金：大人（高校生以上） 2,500 円、小・中学生 1,000 円。未就学児無料。

"无论有没有终止开关，捕捞都是菲尔德和奥本海姆唯一的选择——根本没有时间做前期准备，更不用说提前构思电影了。“我们唯一真正有时间做的事情，就是给生活中那些我们可以托付生命的人打电话，”奥本海姆说道。“我们基本上把各自的‘复仇者联盟’全拉进了这件事里。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个小小的《You Can See Everything》团队包括奥本海姆的老搭档摄影指导大卫·博伦（David Bolen）和制作声音混音师理查德·卡洛斯（Richard Carlos），而菲尔德则叫上了他在《笨蛋 A面》和《诅咒》中的摄像师乔纳森·米歇尔（Jonathan Mitchell），以及自高中起就一直紧密合作的剪辑师亚当·洛克-诺登（Adam Locke-Norden）。", "translated": true}, "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“一共就是7个人走进了伊丽莎白和她的伴侣比利在德尔马住的那栋房子，我们当时根本不知道会发现什么，”奥本海姆说，“内森对这事能不能成持极度怀疑态度，而我显然是从另一个角度出发的：‘我可能正在跟我的电影偶像之一合作，所以我希望这件事能成。我希望它能非常棒。’”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一旦到了实地，奥本海姆便开始担心他和菲尔德并不在同一个频道上。在经历了每天14到16小时的拍摄后，对于这对伴侣的家庭生活，两人有着截然不同的解读——他们既要在其中处理育儿问题，又试图推出他们的新项目：一个由人工智能驱动的、类似 Theranos 2.0 的医疗检测设备。", "paragraph", "text": "“感觉我们突然进入了这样一个地带，有点像[俄罗斯导演安德烈]塔可夫斯基的《潜行者》里的那个禁区，又有点像[塔可夫斯基的另一部电影]《飞向太空》，感觉我们身处这样一个地方：现实的法则和我们所看到的一切，没有任何人能对任何事达成共识，而就在那个时候，我觉得内森[开始看到了一部电影的雏形]，”奥本海姆说。", "translated": true}, "“我们眼前发生了一些时刻，感觉极其有层次且丰富。比如：‘这是一场表演吗？还不是表演？这是一件正在真实发生的事情吗？观察一个以精明骗术闻名的人，有可能捕捉到真实的瞬间吗？’，”奥本海姆说，“我当时绝对是觉得：‘我被这东西激发了活力。我认为这种体验带来的认知失调是极具电影感的。我觉得我们能用这个做出点东西来。’而且我想内森也看到了，并觉得：‘在这些极其暧昧模糊、却又如打鸡蛋这般简单纯粹的时刻里，蕴含着丰富而成熟的养分。’\"", article_text:
Lance Oppenheim had been searching for a project to collaborate on with his cinematic idol Nathan Fielder . The two had become fast friends after Oppenheim reached out to Fielder about his first film “ Some Kind of Heaven ” — he knew Fielder had received a screening link, but when Oppenheim logged into the screening service, he could see the “Nathan for You” creator had only watched a portion of the 85-minute documentary.

“I saw [Nathan’s] email on this screening service, and I just decided to cold-email him,” said Oppenheim while a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast in support of the duo’s “ You Can See Everything .” “I said, ‘Hey, I’m a huge fan of yours. You know, there’s another 40 percent of this movie left. It’s not that long. It’s probably 20 minutes — that’s all you have [left] to finish it.’”

Fielder wrote back saying he had actually finished and enjoyed the then-24-year old director’s Sundance breakout film, and from that point forward, whenever Oppenheim was in Los Angeles, the two future collaborators would get together.

“We’d have these really long hangs, and I was just like, ‘What? Are we becoming really good buddies, a bromance or something?,’” Oppenheim said. He credits “Nathan for You” and Fielder’s early Canadian sketch work on YouTube with making him want to make documentaries. “We’d be out for several hours just talking about life and random things, and I started to realize, ‘Oh, maybe he wants to work with me on something.’ So I started just pitching him ideas.”

A couple of the projects Oppenheim brought to Fielder reached the early planning stages, but nothing took hold. Then, in early 2023, when Oppenheim was in town to shoot a commercial, Fielder — who grew up wanting to be a magician — took him to the Magic Castle.

Recalled Oppenheim of the fateful evening, “The magician asked for a celebrity name, just a random name to the group, and someone raised their hand and said ‘Elizabeth Holmes,’ and a light bulb went off in my head.” Earlier that day, Oppenheim had heard a rumor that Holmes had reached out to A24 about shooting a documentary with her before May 30, 2023, the day the disgraced Theranos founder would begin her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors of her medical testing device. “From what I had heard, A24 was interested and then backtracked because they got a little nervous and just didn’t have a director.”

Assuming the universe was speaking to him when Holmes’ name was injected into their Magic Castle hang, Oppenheim told Fielder about the rumor he’d just heard, and argued, if true, the project could be intriguing for two very different reasons: “First off, why A24? Did she watch ‘Ex Machina,’ or something, and liked it?,” he recalled.

And the second, more substantial, reason: Holmes hadn’t done an on-camera interview since Theranos imploded. The details of said implosion were unearthed by the Wall Street Journal, only to become a fascination for the general public, who couldn’t get enough of the story of the young CEO who conned Silicon Valley out of billions, via a popular podcast, best-selling book (“Bad Blood”), an Alex Gibney documentary , and a scripted Hulu limited series (“ The Dropout “) starring Amanda Seyfried as Holmes.

Fielder agreed, but, according to Oppenheim, worried “that the story been told so many times already.” Regardless, Oppenheim nudged Fielder to call A24 in the morning, and he confirmed the rumors — a deal with Holmes had fallen apart, with only weeks left before she had to report to the Federal Prison Camp (FCP) in Bryan, Texas. It was against this backdrop that Fielder pitched A24 a highly unusual arrangement.

Explained Oppenheim, “Nathan [said to A24], ‘Well, do you think if Lance and I were to go and see if there was something there, would you be comfortable with giving us money and essentially just leaving us alone, and giving us a provision in our deal, whatever the money was, that we could just kill it at any time? If we didn’t find something, we could just throw it all away, we could throw it in the garbage can. And they thankfully agreed.”

Oppenheim said Fielder negotiating a “kill switch” on the project “changed everything.” Fielder remained skeptical there was a movie to be made with Holmes and her partner Billy Evans, who were holed up with their two small children in a Del Mar, California beach cottage with only 34 days — by the time Fielder and Oppenheim arrived — remaining before reporting to the Bryan FCP, but gone was the pressure to figure any of that out.

“This was the first time where I’ve ever been like, ‘Oh, we actually have room to explore something without any pressure of anyone looking [over us],’” said Oppenheim. “ I wish I could have that for every project, because then it really feels like you’re just operating purely out of curiosity. You can essentially fish.”

Regardless of the kill switch, fishing was Fielder and Oppenheim’s only option — there was no time to prep, let alone figure out the movie ahead of time. “All we really had time to do was call the people in our respective lives that we trust with our lives,” said Oppenheim. “We basically brought our individual Avengers into this thing.”

The small “You Can See Everything” team included Oppenheim’s longtime cinematographer David Bolen and production sound mixer Richard Carlos, while Fielder called up his “Nathan for You” and “The Curse” camera operator Jonathan Mitchell, and editor Adam Locke-Norden, who he’d been working closely with since high school.

“It was seven people that [just] went into that house in Del Mar, where Elizabeth and her partner Billy were living, and we didn’t know what we would find,” said Oppenheim. “Nathan was so skeptical about this being anything, and obviously I’m coming at it from the other side, ‘I’m working potentially with one of my cinematic heroes, so I want this to work. I want this to be great.’”

Once on the ground, Oppenheim worried he and Fielder were not on the same page. After 14-to-16 hour days filmming, they had wildly different interpretations of what each had observed of the couple’s domestic life, in which they mixed parenting with trying to launch their new venture, an AI-powered Theranos 2.0-like medical testing device.

“There were things that we were seeing that we could not agree on. Things that we were observing that should have been super simple and very mundane and very boring,” said Oppenheim. “We’d wrap shooting for a day, Nathan and I would talk about it, and he’d be like, ‘That’s not what happened,’ and I’m like, ‘That is what happened. I was watching it on three different monitors. I was watching it with distance. I wasn’t in the conversation [Fielder was the one engaging with Evans and Holmes].’”

The co-directors turned to their trusted crew to settle their debates, but Bolen, Mitchell, and Carlos each had interpretations of their own. Everyone had a different point of view on the isolated domestic life they were laser-focused on capturing.

“It felt like we were suddenly in this zone, almost like the zone in [Russian director Andrei] Tarkovsky’s ‘Stalker,’ it felt a little bit like [another Tarkovsky movie] ‘Solaris,’ it felt like we were in this place that the laws of reality and what we were seeing, no one could agree on anything, and that was the first time where Nathan, I think [started to see a film]” said Oppenheim.

Fielder and Oppenheim realized these divergent interpretations weren’t a problem between the collaborators; rather, the questions they were asking, and disagreeing over, were the film’s concept itself, something they could sink their teeth into.

“There’s these moments that are happening before us that feel extremely layered and dense. Like, ‘Is this a performance? Is it not a performance? Is this a real thing that’s happening? Is it possible to observe an authentic moment with someone who is known for being a master deceiver?,’” said Oppenheim. “I was definitely like, ‘I’m energized by this. I think the cognitive dissonance of this experience is cinematic. I think we can do something with this.’ And I think Nathan saw it and was like, ’There’s something rich and ripe within these moments that are extremely ambiguous, but as simple as someone whisking eggs.’”

According to Oppenheim, it was after this discovery that discussion of the kill switch dissipated: “That was the moment we were like, ‘OK, we have to commit to this. We have to make this work. Let’s just keep going with this process.’”

article_text:
Sometimes, a movie appears seemingly out of nowhere and instantly captures the zeitgeist. In 2026, one of those movies was “ Buddy .”

Casper Kelly’s horror comedy about a ’90s TV show mascot with a dark side captures the nostalgia subversion that made his Adult Swim projects like “Too Many Cooks” into viral hits. But what separates “Buddy” from so many other movies about cuddly villains is the emotional depth lurking below the surface. The many facets of Buddy the Unicorn — his humor, his charisma, his sadism, and his remorse for his actions — allowed Roadside Attractions to mount a unique marketing campaign that introduced audiences to the character before letting them know he had a homicidal streak. The campaign created a false memory that led many of us to wonder if “Buddy” was actually a cancelled TV show we had forgotten about. It ensured that we were invested in the character before we even knew what the film was about.

At IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Summit in Los Angeles, “Buddy” producer Tracy Rosenblum, co-writer Jamie King, and Roadside Attractions head of digital marketing Melissa Yerou joined us for a conversation about the years of behind-the-scenes work that goes into an overnight success.

The project was originally conceived as a way to put Kelly’s distinct brand of comedy into a feature film. King was brought in as a co-writer to help Kelly fit his wild sensibilities into a movie format, and used his recent experience writing Disney movies to ground the story with enough heart to reach a wider audience.

“I knew, as a fan of Casper’s and all of his Adult Swim work, that he would make it really funny. And I knew my friends at BoulderLight would make it really scary. So I thought that if I can help bring that heart element, that checks all three boxes, and that’s what makes a great movie,” King said, adding that he and Kelly worked hard to ensure Buddy came across as a three dimensional character who contained both light and darkness. ““He was always very clear that Buddy was not one of those mascot horror movies you’ve seen before, where Buddy is just a fuzzy version of a slasher villain… He’s someone who could be a good person, but he’s just gone down the wrong road.”

“I resent you calling him a homicidal maniac,” Rosenblum said with a laugh. “He has depth, and he has shame, and he’s not a good guy, but I think that’s what makes him special.”

The character was so thoroughly developed that Yerou and her team could hit the ground running on a marketing campaign. They quickly found success by having Buddy interact with classic ’90s brands on social media, as audiences fell in love with the voice that King and Kelly worked so hard to refine.

“We followed Care Bears and Barney and all these tried and true properties. We just thought ‘What if we had Buddy bust into the conversations, how would they react?’” Yerou said. “At first we were responding to every single comment. We really wanted to heighten the engagement, and at a certain point people were commenting just because they wanted Buddy to respond.” Watch the complete panel in the video above.

IndieWire Future of Filmmaking 2026 Summit is presented by AT&T Untold Stories, an impactful multi-year collaboration between AT&T and Tribeca Festival that awards $1.2 million dollars, mentorship, and comprehensive support to the next generation of filmmakers looking to bring their films to the big screen. For more information, visit here .

title_original: "Für sie waren Kunst und Leben das Gleiche"

Nach ihrem frühen Tod bewahrte und vermittelte ihre Tochter Amrei ihr Werk. Ein Gespräch über hartnäckige Ignoranz und neues Interesse"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "An der Malerin Annemirl Bauer kommt man gerade nur schwer vorbei.
